title: VTTI/VDOT thermal-camera AI wildlife detection pilot on Route 460 near Grundy, Virginia: 97% detection accuracy and a 3 mph average speed drop at activated signs
summary: Drivers slowed by an average of 3 mph near the signs during a one-year trial in Virginia.
account: Gwen Sheldon reported for Virginia Tech on 20 October 2026 on a one-year Virginia Tech Transportation Institute (VTTI) pilot that ended in September 2026. It ran on Route 460 near Grundy in Southwest Virginia, sponsored by the Virginia Department of Transportation (VDOT) as part of the Corridor Q expansion. Eight portable solar-powered trailers with thermal cameras were installed on a 750-meter section of a 14-mile corridor that is home to about 100 elk. AI software from Crosstek analyzed the camera feeds. When wildlife was detected, dynamic message signs told motorists that wildlife had been detected ahead and to slow down. T-Mobile provided 5G and satellite links. The system achieved 97 percent overall accuracy in identifying medium and large wildlife. The initial analysis found an average speed reduction of 3 mph as vehicles approached activated signs. The report gives detection accuracy and driver speeds but no result on collisions or fatalities prevented. WCYB had reported the test on 19 November 2025. Its separate interview with Michelle Earl of VDOT describes animal detection and communication with the message boards. The measured results come from VTTI's own report. WCYB's earlier interview establishes deployment context, not independent verification of those results.
purpose: Detect large wildlife near the roadway and warn approaching drivers in real time to reduce wildlife-vehicle collisions. The measured driver slowdown was the intended response.
system: Thermal-camera wildlife detection with AI video analytics triggering dynamic message signs (cameras and software by Crosstek)
developer: Crosstek (cameras and detection software); system integration and evaluation by Virginia Tech Transportation Institute
deployer: Virginia Department of Transportation with Virginia Tech Transportation Institute
location: Route 460 (Corridor Q) near Grundy, Buchanan County, Virginia, USA
domain: Road safety and wildlife-vehicle collision prevention
taxonomy_note: The documented effect is slower driving at warning signs; collisions avoided are not established.

method.description: Combines the proportions of crash severity from 3,421 elk crash records in five states with Virginia comprehensive costs for those severity categories.

input_references.role: Virginia-specific comprehensive costs by crash severity.
input_references.access_status: Full three-page memorandum read and table 1 visually checked in the preserved copy. The original VDOT URL returned an access error.

input_references.citation: Harmon et al. Crash Costs for Highway Safety Analysis. 2018.
input_references.role: Underlying method for the Virginia comprehensive crash costs.
input_references.access_status: Identified from the original report’s method citation; not independently assessed in this review.

claim_lineage.interpretation: A comprehensive societal valuation, including tangible economic impacts and monetized pain and suffering through quality-adjusted life years. It is not an observed cash loss, payment, or saving produced by the AI pilot.
limitations: California supplied 171 crashes, but only 67 had severity information. Table 12, footnote a treats the remaining 104 as property-damage-only crashes.
The authors apply crash severity proportions from other states; this does not establish how many elk crashes would occur or be prevented on Corridor Q.
No number of crashes avoided by the AI pilot is established, so this unit valuation cannot be multiplied into an AI benefit.

price_basis.basis: VDOT memorandum tables 1–2 label Virginia crash costs as 2020 values. Page 3 states that the adjustment uses 2020 economic indicators.

provenance.basis: Read the original publications and followed the contextual cost claim through the feasibility study, original calculation, table footnotes, and cited VDOT cost memorandum. The memorandum establishes the 2020 price basis. Uninspected underlying federal methodology and raw crash data remain identified as inputs, not independently reproduced evidence.
